text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past interactions as continuing demand for broadly related products or entertainment, with insufficient distinction between general interest and current intent.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they follow a specific recent interest, such as a closely connected artist, musical style, or story theme.",
    "Practical recommendations succeed when they extend an existing activity or setup with a clearly useful capability."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad category or brand relationships compete with stronger connections to the user's recent purpose, preferred sound, or specific task.",
    "Similar purchases are treated as evidence of further demand even when recommendations duplicate functions or supplies the user already owns.",
    "Specialized products are suggested without sufficient evidence of the required project, compatibility, dimensions, or quantity need."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared categories, brands, materials, or terminology are treated as stronger evidence of relevance than shared purpose.",
    "Occasional or older interactions are extended into broad ongoing preferences that do not consistently match current choices."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Repeated recent behavior and specific item-to-item connections provide stronger evidence of current intent than broad historical similarity.",
    "Existing ownership, functional compatibility, and incremental usefulness determine whether a related product is worth choosing.",
    "Entertainment choices depend on particular tone, musical qualities, and seasonal context rather than genre membership alone."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top-ranked recommendations too often have a broad relationship to past behavior without a sufficiently specific, timely reason to choose them now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "Track the proportion of top-ranked items users would choose now, distinguishing immediate choices from general-interest matches.",
    "Track rejection frequency for duplicate functionality, unsupported project assumptions, and compatibility or quantity mismatches.",
    "Compare acceptance of recommendations connected to repeated recent behavior with those supported mainly by broad category or brand similarity.",
    "Track judgments of insufficient information separately from explicit preference mismatches, particularly when item identities are unavailable."
  ]
}
